transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because my sleep has basically fallen apart. I lie in bed for hours, laptop closed, but I’m still going over work deadlines, tuition payments, and class assignments in my head. And when I do sleep, I wake up feeling like I never really shut off.
How long has this sleep problem been going on—days, weeks, or longer?
About a year and three months now—since I started an evening graduate certificate program while still working my full-time analyst job.

Aside from the nights when you're trying to sleep, do you find yourself worrying excessively about things like work, finances, or school on most days, and do you feel like you can't control that worry?

Yes. I’ll try to tell myself to stop and just focus on one thing, but then one worry turns into another. Before I know it, I’m checking my calendar, my budget, and my assignments over and over instead of actually getting anything done. It feels really hard to shut it off.
Besides the worry and sleep trouble, have you noticed other symptoms like feeling restless or on edge, muscle tension, irritability, or trouble concentrating during the day?

Yes, concentrating has been really difficult. I’ll stare at a financial model or a reading for class and realize I’ve read the same paragraph five times without taking it in, because my mind is already going through everything that could go wrong.
Do you often feel physically restless, keyed up, or notice muscle tension in your body during the day?
I’m not really sure what counts as muscle tension. I do feel like I have a hard time settling down during the day, but I haven’t specifically noticed anything else.
Are there nights when you don't feel particularly worried about work or school, but you still have trouble falling or staying asleep?
Even when I’m trying not to think about work or school, I still lie there for a long time before I fall asleep. And when I do sleep, I wake up feeling like my mind never really shut off.
On nights when you actually sleep well and feel rested the next day, do you still find yourself excessively worrying about work, finances, or school?
Yes. Even if I’ve slept okay, my mind still jumps between work, the cost of school, and what my family might think. Small things can feel like they could mess up my whole future.
During times when you're away from work and school obligations, like a weekend or vacation, do you still have trouble falling or staying asleep?

Yes. Even when I’m away from work or school, I can lie in bed for hours with everything turned off, still going over deadlines, tuition, or assignments in my head. And when I do sleep, I wake up feeling like I never really switched off.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports excessive, difficult-to-control worry about multiple domains (work, finances, school, family expectations) present for over a year, occurring independent of sleep quality and persisting even during time off (weekends, breaks), indicating the worry is not solely reactive to a specific stressor or situation. Associated symptoms include sleep disturbance (initial insomnia, non-restorative sleep), concentration difficulty, and subjective restlessness/inability to settle down. The chronicity (>6 months), pervasiveness across contexts, and multiple associated somatic/cognitive symptoms support Generalized Anxiety Disorder over a primary sleep disorder (insomnia is secondary to worry, not independent) or adjustment disorder (symptoms persist beyond and independent of the specific stressor context).
